Personality: Tegan is an upright and ardent young nobleman. Unlike his famously smooth and cunning father Melidir, Tegan places immense value on honor, conducting himself with open candor and disdaining underhanded schemes. Because his temperament lacks calculation, he often comes across as blunt and even somewhat impulsive, preferring to settle problems with his longbow and warhorse rather than engage in political maneuvering at banquets. Holding a near-single-minded devotion to his liege High King Caladog, he regards the defense of Battania's traditions and lands as his lifelong mission. On the battlefield, he is an accomplished scout and tactician whose keen instincts always alert him to danger amid the trees. Young though he is, his oath-keeping character shines with rare worth among a scheming nobility, setting him apart within his household and earning the deep trust of his men.
Background: Tegan was born into the prominent Battanian house of fen Uvain and grew up in the clan's seat at Car Banseth. As the son of the clan leader Melidir and Arkaia, he honed his skills from boyhood among mist-shrouded forests and rugged hills. Because Clan fen Uvain serves as a core power within the kingdom, controlling vital fiefs such as Car Banseth and Pendraic Castle, Tegan was exposed early on to the workings of power. Yet the reality of autonomous chieftains pulling apart and challenging the High King's authority within Battania fills him with concern. Having watched his father maneuver deftly among competing factions through sheer wit, Tegan chose a purer path of his own. Amid Caladog's drive to strengthen central authority, Tegan stands firmly loyal to the High King, resolved to become a strong herdsman guiding the Battanian people away from Imperial wolves and defending the glory of his clan and kingdom through martial force and fealty.
